results.controlIntent: a. Internal system clocks are used to generate time stamps for audit records; and b. Time stamps recorded for audit records meet [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] and use Coordinated Universal Time, have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time, or include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint use ISO 8601 timestamps with the 'Z' (UTC) suffix (e.g., '2025-12-01T11:00:00Z' and '2026-03-15T14:22:00Z'). This satisfies AU-8.v2(b)'s requirement to use Coordinated Universal Time. Timestamps are generated by AWS CloudTrail's internal system clocks, satisfying AU-8.v2(a). The granularity is second-level (HH:MM:SS), which is substantively adequate for audit purposes. Confidence is medium rather than high because no organization-defined granularity policy document was available to confirm the required precision level — it is possible the organization mandates sub-second (millisecond) granularity, which these records do not provide. The change-control anomalies noted in the event payloads are relevant to other controls (e.g., CM-3), not AU-8.
gaps: No organization-defined time-stamp granularity policy was available to confirm whether second-level precision meets the stated requirement — sub-second (millisecond) granularity may be mandated.
No AWS Config or CloudWatch evidence was available to confirm NTP/clock synchronization configuration for the underlying compute infrastructure.
Only two CloudTrail events were retrieved; a broader sample across the full audit log would increase confidence.
